transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

When there’s a line or a process, I just can’t seem to wait my turn without jumping ahead or changing plans, and it keeps messing up our money and appointments. It's gotten to the point where it's putting my family's finances in a really bad spot, and I knew I had to get some help.
When you jump ahead or change plans, is it mainly because you feel driven to do it impulsively, or because you are deliberately arguing, defying rules, or refusing requests from others?

Oh, it's definitely not because I want to break rules or argue with anyone. It's just this really antsy, impatient feeling where I act before I even think, and I just can't seem to hold myself back. I'm not trying to be difficult, my body just moves before my brain has a chance to stop it.

Do you also act impulsively in other areas, like spending money, interrupting others, making quick decisions, or doing risky things without thinking first? Or is it mainly this impatience with waiting and lines?

Yes, it definitely goes beyond just waiting in lines. I constantly find myself interrupting people, blurting out answers or finishing their sentences during meetings and appointments before they're even done speaking. I also make impulsive little purchases that completely ruin our budget spreadsheets and cause us a lot of financial strain.
Did these impulsive and interrupting behaviors start in childhood or early adolescence, and have they been present in more than one setting (such as home, school, and work)?

Yes, they definitely started way back in elementary school; my teachers were always calling my mom because I couldn't stay in my seat, blurted things out, and kept getting sent to the hallway. It has always been an issue in different places, from school back then to now at home with my family, at church, and at the community center.
Do you also have trouble paying attention to details, staying focused, or finishing tasks because your mind wanders or you get distracted easily?

Yes, I really struggle with staying focused and finishing tasks. When I try to go over bills or paperwork, my mind quickly drifts off to a song in my head or the birds outside, and I have to keep starting over. I also get easily sidetracked by conversations or other things when I'm trying to get things done, so I often end up leaving tasks half-finished.
Do you also have clear symptoms of hyperactivity, such as feeling restless, unable to stay seated, fidgeting a lot, or needing to move around constantly?

Yes, absolutely. I constantly have this "buzzing" feeling inside that makes me feel restless, and my legs are always bouncing or my fingers tapping during church or meetings. It gets so bad that I can't even stay in my seat during long waits at the benefits office and just have to get up and pace around.
Do you often lose your temper, argue with people, deliberately refuse to do what they ask, or feel resentful or spiteful toward them?

No, not at all, I don't really lose my temper or argue with people, and I never refuse to do things out of spite. If I don't follow through on what my wife or others ask, it's strictly because I get sidetracked or impatient, not because I'm trying to be defiant or resentful.
Do you ever have periods of needing much less sleep than usual and still feeling unusually energized or overly confident, or is your sleep generally normal?

I don't really have times where I need way less sleep or feel overly confident, and my sleep is generally normal. Sometimes it can just be hard to wind down at night because my body is still feeling so restless and full of energy. Other than that, I don't experience those kinds of highs or bursts of extra energy.
Before age 12, did these attention, impulsivity, and restlessness symptoms cause problems at school or at home, and are they still clearly causing problems in your daily life now?

Yes, they definitely did; back in elementary school, my teachers were constantly calling my mom because I couldn't stay in my seat, blurted things out, and kept getting sent to the hallway. Today, it's still causing huge problems because my inability to sit still, wait my turn, or follow through has led to missed appointments, lost benefits, and budget mistakes. It has gotten so bad that we are now at real risk of falling behind on our rent.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, predominantly hyperactive/impulsive presentation, with onset in childhood, symptoms across multiple settings, and current clinically significant impairment. He confirmed persistent impulsivity, difficulty waiting his turn, interrupting/blurted speech, fidgeting/restlessness, inability to stay seated, and distractibility with unfinished tasks. He explicitly denied oppositional, defiant, or manic symptoms.
